messages:
Jordan (support): Acme support ticket #12345 — they're seeing repeated 503/500s from the hosted inference endpoint in us-west-2 starting ~02:10 UTC. Happens for a few customers but Acme is on our highest-volume workload. They say requests either time out or return 'upstream worker error'. They included a sample request id: req_0a7f3c. Posting logs they attached.

ops-bot: Incident created: incidents/1945678901, severity: high, region: us-west-2. Pager duty: sent to oncall.

Maya (sre): Taking this. Jordan — can you paste the exact request payload (redact PII) and the raw worker logs for req_0a7f3c? Any correlation with model or batch size?

Jordan (support): Sample request headers/body (redacted):
```json
{"model":"gpt-large-quantized-4bit","input_tokens":8200,"batch_size":4,"max_tokens":1024,"route":"hosted/default"}
```
Attached log snippet from the customer's client side and our gateway around that time:
```
2026-03-15T02:10:12Z gateway: request=req_0a7f3c forwarded to upstream worker=wrk-22
2026-03-15T02:10:14Z wrk-22: ERROR RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 1.12 GiB (requested 1207147264 bytes)
2026-03-15T02:10:14Z wrk-22: aborting process, signal 6
2026-03-15T02:10:15Z kubelet: container "inference-wrk-22" terminated with exit code 134
2026-03-15T02:10:17Z gateway: upstream worker wrk-22 not healthy -> returning 503 to client
```

Asha (mlops): I'm seeing a very similar pattern on infra metrics — GPU memory climbs steadily to ~99% then the process is killed. This is a quantized model but the token sequence is very long (8200 tokens). Our default KV-cache growth plus batching can spike VRAM.

Bryan (infra): Which kernel and allocator? Any segfault frames? If it's pure OOM that's one path; but we also had two SIGSEGVs last week with the same model when certain attention kernels run. Check the worker logs for a native stack.

Jordan (support): Added raw worker core excerpt they provided: 
```
Fatal signal 11 (SIGSEGV), code 1, fault addr 0x7ffdeadbeef
#0 0x7f9c1a2b in torch::some_function at /opt/conda/lib/python3.9/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch.so
#1 0x55aab4a in attention_kernel::run
```
So not pure OOM in that trace — looks like a segfault inside the attention kernel after high memory pressure.

Maya (sre): OK two failure modes: (A) CUDA OOM -> controlled abort; (B) kernel-level SIGSEGV after memory fragmentation or allocator bug. Both lead to container restart -> gateway 503/500. Short-term mitigations: disable batching for this customer route + force a lower max_tokens; long-term: patch allocator or pin to a different kernel.

Bryan (infra): For immediate mitigation I'm going to add a per-route override to disabled batching and a hard max_tokens 512 for Acme via the routing API. Command I used:
```bash
# temporary override
curl -X POST "https://console.redwood.ai/v1/routes/overrides" -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"route":"acme-prod","batching":false,"max_tokens":512,"model":"gpt-medium-v2"}'
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: Route override applied: route=acme-prod, batching=false, model=gpt-medium-v2, expire=2026-03-15T04:00:00Z.

Asha (mlops): Reproduced locally with a synthetic request: long sequence (~8k tokens) + batch_size=4 -> GPU memory climbs and fragmentation appears before OOM. Repro steps I used:
1) spin a worker with model gpt-large-quantized-4bit on a gpus with 40GB VRAM
2) send the following curl: 
```bash
curl -X POST https://hosted.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST_KEY" -d '{"model":"gpt-large-quantized-4bit","input": "<8k_tokens>", "batch_size":4}'
```
Observed: memory usage trajectory -> 65% -> 88% -> 99% -> allocator error or SIGSEGV.

Maya (sre): Good repro. Notes: the quantized 4-bit kernel we ship has known issues with long KV cache growth in sequences >6k tokens under batching. We did not hit this in perf tests because sequence distribution skew is rare, but customers with chat logs can hit it.

Jordan (support): Customer responded: the workaround (smaller model + disabled batching) reduced errors to zero for the last 30 min. They're asking for a fix and timeline.

Bryan (infra): Next steps:
- Short: Keep route override for Acme until EOD; manual check-in at 04:00 UTC.
- Medium: Create AB test on a patched allocator branch that caps prefetch memory for KV cache (Asha + Bryan).
- Long: Add a per-model guard that refuses requests which would exceed estimated memory budget (reject with 4xx or auto-fallback to smaller model).

Asha (mlops): I'll open a changelist to add an early-memory-estimation step and an opt-in allocator patch. Also will add an automatic 'fallback to smaller model' policy for routes that hit repeated OOMs.

Maya (sre): I'll postmortem if the override remains >2 hours. For now severity reduced to medium since no new errors for Acme after override. Keep monitoring us-west-2.

Jordan (support): Customer updated and very grateful for the fast mitigation. They've requested a follow-up email summarizing root cause and fixes planned. I'll draft the email after we have the postmortem notes. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Monitoring: no 5xx spikes in us-west-2 for last 20m. Alert will escalate if errors > 5/min.

Maya (sre): Thanks team — assigning action items: Asha (allocator + fallback feature), Bryan (patch branch + test infra), Jordan (customer comms). I'll own the incident doc and RCA when we have builds validated.

Jordan (support): Note for the doc: include request_id req_0a7f3c, worker wrk-22, node ip 10.11.12.22, and timestamps.

Bryan (infra): saving logs to s3://redwood-incident-logs/1945678901/ and kicking off CI run for allocator patch. Will ping here when builds land.

Asha (mlops): CI run started for allocator branch. Reproducer tests added to the e2e suite.

Maya (sre): Closing thread for now — reopening if we see recurrence.
